uncited: All methods in this family share the mechanism of mapping 6D input coordinates to 4D output values using a differentiable neural network, allowing the radiance field to be optimized end-to-end through the volumetric rendering integral.
Raw coordinates $\mathbf{x}$ and $\mathbf{d}$ are rarely used directly due to the spectral bias of MLPs, which struggle to fit high-frequency details.
**Density Network:** Takes the encoded position $\gamma(\mathbf{x})$ as input.

**Color Network:** Takes the encoded position $\gamma(\mathbf{x})$, the raw viewing direction $\mathbf{d}$, and the intermediate feature vector from the density network (usually the output of the last hidden layer before the density head) as input.
During training, rays are sampled at points $\mathbf{x}_i$ along the ray.
